Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday. Procurement here wants a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out legal and procurement sequencing so we can get our pilot started by mid-November. Key asks from our side:

- Confirmation of the order: sequence MSA -> DPA -> order form (we need clarity on whether order form can precede DPA in practice).
- SOC 2 / security evidence for the pilot environment and any expected timelines for KMS/HSM details.
- Acceptance testing definition and acceptance gate owners (we have a 2-week pilot acceptance window).
- Target billing start date (upon signature vs upon acceptance).

Can you send a MAP draft with suggested dates and responsible owners? Procurement would like a single page they can attach to their internal approval.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,

Hi Elena — thanks, and great meeting yesterday.

Attached is a one-page MAP draft (Cardinal_MAP_v1.pdf) that lays out our recommended sequencing and target dates for a mid-November pilot start. High-level summary below:

- Week of Oct 4: Legal to review MSA; sales to finalize order form terms. (Owner: Karthik / Vanessa)
- Oct 11: MSA redlines exchanged & DPA checklist reviewed; SOC 2 evidence shared (Owner: Redwood Legal / Security)
- Oct 18: Procurement to issue PO for pilot, or confirm PO target date (Owner: Cardinal Procurement)
- Oct 22–Nov 4: 2-week pilot window (acceptance tests defined in MAP appendix). Acceptance gate: Cardinal QA sign-off.
- Nov 5: Production onboarding (if pilot accepted) and billing start: we recommend billing begin upon acceptance sign-off to avoid billing disputes.

Notes / sequencing guidance:
- Our suggested order is sign MSA (paper signature) -> DPA executed in parallel (we can provision pilot access under mutual NDA while DPA is finalized but SOC2 controls must be provided before data ingress).
- Order form can be prepared and routed internally but procurement often needs the final order form to cut a PO; to keep timeline tight we recommend finalizing a draft order form by Oct 11 so procurement has time to review.

I’ve CC'd Vanessa for commercial items and Karthik for legal sequencing. Karthik — any redline timing concerns on your side?

Attachments: Cardinal_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft), MAP appendix (acceptance criteria).

Thanks — I can update the MAP with dates once we have procurement's PO target.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 2:22 PM Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ve CC'd Vanessa for commercial items and Karthik for legal sequencing. Karthik — any redline timing concerns on your side?

Elena / team — quick legal note and proposed sequencing so procurement has visibility.

1) MSA redlines: I’ve attached suggested redlines (redlines_msa_20261005.docx). Key asks from our side: a standard liability cap tied to fees paid in 12 months, explicit pilot acceptance gating so the order form only moves to production if acceptance criteria are met.
2) DPA: We recommend executing the DPA either concurrent with MSA or immediately after MSA signature. To avoid blocking the pilot, Redwood can provide SOC 2 artifact set (scope and controls) and a temporary data handling addendum for the pilot period — this avoids delaying onboarding while DPA legalese is being finalized.
3) Order form: Commercial should own the final order form, but legal needs a clear clause in the MSA that the order form's effective date = acceptance sign-off if the customer prefers that. Alternatively, we can allow billing start on signature if Cardinal prefers cashflow to start earlier; we should confirm.

Timeline risks: If Cardinal procurement requires a fully executed DPA before any access, we will need an expedited legal review (2–3 business days after redline receipt).

I’ll iterate on the attached redlines Tuesday and can provide a tracked version for Cardinal's counsel.

–Karthik
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Billing start: Redwood prefers billing upon acceptance to align incentives. If Cardinal needs billing upon signed order form for PO reasons, we can accommodate for the pilot with a capped pilot invoice and crediting if acceptance fails.
- PO timing: Can procurement confirm a target PO issue date? If we aim for a pilot kickoff week of Oct 25 (access provisioned) we would need PO by Oct 18 to meet internal finance cutoffs.
- Order form: I’ve attached an editable orderform draft internally; we’ll share a cleaned copy for Cardinal by Oct 11.

Elena — is Oct 18 a realistic PO date from your side? If not, what does procurement need to get there?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
